survivors_flagged.one_line: Two-way break-up (bank to CommerceOne for $8.11 cash plus 0.2215 new-holdco shares; fintech to Smith Ventures). Shareholder votes and HSR are done; Fed/AL/UT bank approvals are pending and the close slipped to Q1-2027. Complex arb with a stub, but it is late-arc and widely known.

Strathcona deal (Nov 8): holders elect C$11 cash or 0.25 SCR shares, no proration. WEF (72%) takes stock and supports the deal. Majority-of-minority votes in Jan 2027, close early 2027. The premium already jumped 38%, so check the spread against C$11 and the SCR ratio before entering.

Amazon deal at $90 cash or 0.321 AMZN (capped at $90). Written consent already done and FCC approved 2026-10-27. Close guided to 2027 and tied to deployment milestones, with up to $110M downward adjustment. Px 86.13 = ~4.5% gross spread; the stock leg is worth ~$82.6 at AMZN 257. Plain arb, late-arc, no mispricing edge.

verified.catalyst: Green Dot is being split two ways. The bank goes to CommerceOne, and each GDOT share gets $8.11 cash plus 0.2215 shares of the new listed bank holding company. The non-bank fintech business goes to Smith Ventures for $690M cash. The deal closes once the Fed, the Alabama State Banking Department and the Utah Department of Financial Institutions approve it.
verified.dated_milestone: Both companies' shareholders approved on 2026-06-23. Applications were filed 2026-02-20. The Q3-2026 release guides to a close by Q1-2027. Next marker: if approvals arrive before 2026-12-21, the 2026 annual meeting is cancelled, so watch for a regulatory-approval 8-K by about mid-Dec 2026. The backstop is the Q1-2027 close.
verified.instrument: GDOT common (NYSE), $11.20 on 2026-11-20. Long GDOT alone means owning $8.11 cash plus an implied stub of $3.09 (implied $13.95 per new-holdco share). A hedge is not possible because the new holdco does not trade yet.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: named counterparties CommerceOne Financial and Smith Ventures. G2 yes: signed merger agreement, shareholder votes done, $8.11 cash per share is contractual. G3 partial: the cash leg is specific, but the stub value (0.2215 new-holdco shares) is derived, not contractual. Management's $14.23-$19.18 range rests on an assumed 1.0x-1.8x tangible-book multiple from Nov 2025. I did not re-derive it.
verified.edge: M-L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base ($10.95 close on 2025-11-20, before the 2025-11-23 announcement) to $11.20 today is only +2.3%. So this is not harvested in the VISN sense, and the downside if the deal breaks looks like roughly the old $10.6-11.0 range. Remaining upside depends entirely on the unverified stub. At management's 1.0x TBV floor ($14.23) it is +27%. If the new holdco trades at 0.6x TBV (about $11.78) it is about +5%. At today's implied stub (about 0.5x of management's TBV figure) it is 0%. The market is discounting either a weak bank franchise or an approval delay, and three slips (Q2, then Q3-2026, then Q1-2027) suggest regulators have real friction. The setup is widely known.
verified.primary_source: GDOT Q3-2026 earnings release (finviz/BusinessWire, Nov 2026): close expected by Q1-2027, Fed/AL/UT approvals pending. Joint shareholder-approval press release, 2026-06-23. 2025-11-23 deal announcement and Form 425 (sec.gov, Nov 2025): $8.11 cash + 0.2215 shares, implied $14.23-$19.18 at 1.0x-1.8x TBV. FMP quote 2026-11-20: $11.20. FMP EOD prices: $10.95 on 2025-11-20, the pre-announcement base.
verified.analysis: The deal is real and late-stage (votes done, HSR done). Only the bank approvals remain, and the close has already slipped three times, to Q1-2027. The $8.11 cash is locked in. The rest of the upside sits in a stub whose value is management's Nov-2025 tangible-book multiple, never re-derived from the current 10-Q (bank tangible book after the $155M capital injection and the ~$65M debt payoff, and how much the bank's deposits depend on the departing fintech business). Under the numerator-provenance rule I scored the equity, not the event, and capped at 4. Next step: before upgrading, pull the Q3-2026 10-Q / S-4/A pro-forma tangible book per new-holdco share and the reason for the regulatory delay. A 2024-era Fed enforcement action on the bank is a plausible cause, unverified.

verified.catalyst: Strathcona (SCR.TO) is buying Greenfire for C$11.00 cash or 0.25 SCR shares per GFR share, with no proration; WEF (72% of GFR, 57% of SCR) supports the deal and elects shares; majority-of-minority votes are expected in January 2027 and closing early 2027.
verified.dated_milestone: Announced 2026-11-08. Joint circular mailing late Nov-2026. Next date: special meetings at both companies, January 2027 (MI 61-101 majority of minority plus two-thirds). Close shortly after, early 2027, subject to court and regulatory approval.
verified.instrument: GFR.TO common (TSX) / GFR (NYSE). There is no spread to capture: the stock trades at the C$11.00 cash option.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 (named counterparty: Strathcona, with WEF's support agreement) and G2 (signed definitive agreement, fixed C$11 cash with no proration). G3 fails: no currently unpriced figure remains, because the cash price is fully reflected at C$11.00.
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base (Nov 6 close about C$7.91) to today's C$11.00 is +39%. Remaining capture to the C$11.00 cash option is about 0.0% (GFR.TO last C$11.00, day high 11.025). The share option is worth 0.25 x C$37.60 = C$9.40, about 15% BELOW market. Upside comes only from a free call on SCR above about C$44.00 (+17%) before elections close. Downside is a deal break back toward the C$8 area (about -28%).
verified.primary_source: Strathcona Resources press release 'Strathcona Resources Ltd. Announces Agreement to Acquire Greenfire Resources Ltd.', 2026-11-08 (via BOE Report); FMP batch-quote GFR.TO C$11.00 / SCR.TO C$37.60 / GFR US$7.67, as of 2026-11-20
verified.analysis: The deal is real, signed and dated, and the controlling holder (WEF, 72%) supports it, so the event passes on quality. But GFR.TO trades exactly at the C$11 cash consideration, with no time value for a close roughly 2-3 months away, so the event is about 100% harvested. Entering now earns about 0% gross (negative after carry) against about -28% break risk. The only optionality is the 0.25 SCR election, which is out of the money (C$9.40 vs C$11) and would need SCR above about C$44. Gaps: the termination fee amount is undisclosed, and the cash leg depends on Strathcona's reserves-based credit facility, which the filing names as a risk factor (no formal financing condition). One older article describes an earlier hostile WEF approach; the current release supersedes it with a signed support agreement.

verified.catalyst: Amazon is buying Globalstar for $90 cash or 0.3210 AMZN per share (stock leg capped at $90). Cash elections are prorated to a 40% cap. Closing is guided to 2027 and depends on HIBLEO-4 replacement-satellite milestones and the remaining approvals, with up to $110M of downward adjustment.
verified.dated_milestone: Announced 2026-04-14. Written consent from about 58% of the vote has already been given. FCC approval was reported 2026-10-27/28. Next: Amazon's S-4 becoming effective, the information statement, the satellite milestones and the remaining foreign-investment approvals. Close is guided only to "2027", with no specific date.
verified.instrument: GSAT common (86.13, 2026-11-20). There is no clean hedge, because the $90 cap removes AMZN upside above about $280.4.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes (Amazon is the named counterparty). G2 yes (signed merger agreement at $90 cash / 0.3210 AMZN). G3 no: no unpriced figure remains, and the prorated consideration is already at or below the current price.
verified.edge: L. (a) Run-up: the pre-catalyst base is about $68.7 (the 2026-04-01 close implied by Reuters' 31% premium; the 2026-04-13 close was $72.89). To 86.13 that is +25% (+18% from the 04-13 close). (b) Remaining: with the 40% cash cap and AMZN at 257.37, blended value is 0.4x90 + 0.6x82.62 = $85.57, which is -0.6% vs today. The best case is $90 (+4.5% gross over roughly 12 months or more) and needs AMZN at or above about $280. The event is real and contractual, but already fully harvested.
verified.primary_source: Amazon press release "Amazon to acquire Globalstar and expand Amazon Leo satellite network" (press.aboutamazon.com, 2026-04-14). TIKR/Stocktwits on FCC approval (updated 2026-10-28). FMP batch-quote GSAT 86.13 / AMZN 257.37 (2026-11-20).
verified.analysis: The deal itself checks out: Amazon is the counterparty, written consent is done, and FCC approval was reported in late October 2026. The triage flag's "4.5% gross spread" is wrong. Because cash elections are prorated to 40%, an arb holder receives a blend worth about $85.57 at AMZN 257, which is below the 86.13 price. The position is really a long-AMZN option capped at $90, with timing and milestone risk (up to $110M downward adjustment, 2027 close with no date). The 40% cash cap comes from deal summaries (Barchart, Amazon press, 2026-04) and should be checked against the merger agreement or S-4. There is no derived numerator to check, since the consideration is contractual. The event has been nearly fully harvested since the April announcement, so the score is capped at 4 and set lower because the expected residual is near zero or negative.
